hero.headline: School bus driver arrested in Treasure Coast after second student comes forward with allegations
hero.body:
A Florida school bus driver has been arrested following allegations from a second student. The arrest comes after an initial complaint led to an investigation that has now expanded with additional allegations of lewd and lascivious molestation.

The second victim came forward after the initial arrest, prompting authorities to file additional charges. The case involves allegations of inappropriate conduct toward students who rode the school bus. Law enforcement officials took the driver into custody following the second complaint.

The arrest raises serious concerns for parents and school officials across the Treasure Coast region. School districts rely on bus drivers to safely transport thousands of students daily, and allegations of this nature prompt immediate action from both law enforcement and school administrators.

The investigation remains active as authorities work to determine if there may be additional victims. School officials are cooperating with law enforcement as the criminal case moves forward through the judicial system.

cards.headline: Body of suspect found after double homicide at Vero Beach library
cards.body:
The body of a suspect who killed his wife and another man at a Vero Beach library has been found, authorities report. The suspect had escaped into the ocean following the deadly incident at the library.

The double homicide occurred at a Vero Beach library facility, where the suspect killed his wife and one other man before fleeing the scene. Law enforcement pursued the suspect, who entered the ocean in an apparent escape attempt.

Search efforts by authorities focused on the coastal area where the suspect was last seen entering the water. The recovery of the suspect's body brings the manhunt to a close, though the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the killings continues.

The incident marks a tragic event for the Vero Beach community. The library serves as a public gathering place for residents throughout Indian River County, and the violent incident has impacted staff and patrons who use the facility regularly.

cards.headline: Five hospitalized after multi-vehicle crash, fire on I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: Five people were taken to hospitals Monday night after a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 northbound near Stuart sparked a vehicle fire, according to Martin.
cards.body:
Five people were taken to hospitals Monday night after a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 northbound near Stuart sparked a vehicle fire, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. The collision occurred just before 10 p.m. on I-95 northbound near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park.

Martin County Fire Rescue crews arrived to find one of the vehicles on fire and quickly extinguished the flames. Two people suffered traumatic injuries and were transported to the hospital, while three others sustained minor injuries and were also taken for medical treatment.

All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed while law enforcement investigated the crash. The closure affected traffic through the night as investigators worked to determine what caused the collision.

As of Tuesday morning, all lanes have reopened. The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the crash.

cards.headline: Second alleged victim comes forward in St. Lucie County bus driver molestation case
cards.teaser: A second alleged victim has come forward in a molestation case involving a St. Lucie County school bus driver, expanding the scope of the investigation.
cards.body:
A second alleged victim has stepped forward in a molestation investigation involving a school bus driver in St. Lucie County. The new allegation adds another dimension to a case that has already raised concerns among parents and school officials across the county.

The case involves a bus driver who transports students in St. Lucie County, which includes Port St. Lucie and Fort Pierce. School bus drivers are entrusted with the safety and wellbeing of children during their daily commutes to and from school, making allegations of abuse particularly troubling for families throughout the community.

The investigation continues as authorities work to determine the full extent of the allegations. St. Lucie County schools serve thousands of students who rely on bus transportation each day, and cases like this highlight the importance of thorough background checks and ongoing supervision of school employees who work directly with children.

cards.headline: Florida Legislature approves property tax cut amendment for November ballot
cards.body:
The Florida Legislature completed its special session Tuesday by approving a tweaked version of Governor Ron DeSantis's proposed property tax cut constitutional amendment. The measure will now go before Florida voters in November.

Lawmakers reconvened for the second day of the special session focused solely on property taxes. The Legislature made modifications to the governor's original proposal before advancing it to a floor vote. Both chambers approved the amended version Tuesday afternoon, sending the constitutional amendment to the ballot for statewide consideration.

The special session brought together members from across Florida to address property tax concerns affecting homeowners and businesses statewide. The National Federation of Independent Business, whose members represent every industry in Florida, has been tracking the legislative developments. Business owners and property owners across the state have been watching the session closely as property tax relief measures could affect their bottom lines.

Florida voters will have the final say on the property tax amendment when they head to the polls in November. Constitutional amendments in Florida require voter approval to take effect. The outcome of the vote will determine whether property tax cuts become part of the state constitution, potentially affecting tax bills for millions of Florida property owners. The Legislature's completion of the special session marks a significant step in the process, though the ultimate decision now rests with the electorate.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie daughter charged with attempted murder after setting fire to bedroom door with mother inside
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman faces charges of attempted murder, arson and resisting arrest after police say she set fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was trapped inside Sunday night. Michelle Picard, 26, is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on $510,000 bond following the incident in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard.

Port St. Lucie Police Department officers responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire around 9:05 p.m. Sunday. The victim noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire, according to police. Investigators say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames.

The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background. Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her, but she resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg. Another officer required treatment for smoke inhalation. Both officers were treated at a local hospital and released. The victim was also hospitalized for treatment of injuries sustained during the incident.

Fire investigators from the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Criminal Investigations Division, Crime Scene Investigators, St. Lucie County Fire District and the State Fire Marshal's Office determined the blaze was intentionally set. The fire damaged the residence, prompting the American Red Cross to assist the victim with temporary housing and support services. Police emphasized this was an isolated domestic incident and there is no ongoing threat to the community.

cards.headline: North Miami man arrested after attempted armed kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church
cards.teaser: A 64-year-old man faces multiple felony charges after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman at gunpoint in a Port St. Lucie church parking lot Sunday morning. Witnesses intervened to stop the incident.
cards.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman in the parking lot of First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard. The incident unfolded around 10:49 a.m. Sunday when Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached her despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

Police say Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim through the parking lot and physically restraining her.

Zamora was located and arrested without incident Sunday evening at a residence in Hialeah by Port St. Lucie Police and U.S. Marshals. The investigation revealed Zamora is a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Zamora faces five felony charges, including attempted kidnapping with a firearm, aggravated assault and battery of a person over 65. He is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on a $745,000 bond.

hero.headline: Downtown Fort Pierce visitors now face hefty citations for parking more than 2 hours
hero.body:
Visitors to downtown Fort Pierce now face expensive parking citations if they stay longer than two hours. The city has begun issuing hefty fines to drivers who exceed the time limit in downtown parking areas.

The new enforcement affects anyone parking in the downtown district, including shoppers, diners, and people visiting local businesses. The citations carry substantial financial penalties for drivers who overstay the two-hour limit.

The stricter parking enforcement comes as Fort Pierce works to manage parking availability in its downtown area. Downtown business districts across Florida have grappled with balancing adequate parking for customers while preventing spaces from being occupied all day by employees or others.

The enforcement policy aims to increase parking turnover and ensure more visitors can find available spaces when they come downtown. Drivers planning to visit downtown Fort Pierce for extended periods should be aware of the two-hour limit and plan accordingly to avoid citations.

cards.headline: Vero Beach approves $190,000 for new Iris Lane sidewalk
cards.teaser: The city of Vero Beach has approved spending $190,000 to build a sidewalk on Iris Lane, improving pedestrian safety in the neighborhood.
cards.body:
Vero Beach officials have approved a $190,000 project to construct a new sidewalk along Iris Lane. The approval came during a recent city meeting as part of ongoing infrastructure improvements throughout the community.

The sidewalk project addresses pedestrian safety concerns on Iris Lane, where residents currently lack a safe walking path. The $190,000 budget will cover construction costs for the new pedestrian infrastructure.

Sidewalk projects like this one are part of Vero Beach's broader efforts to improve walkability and safety in residential neighborhoods. The city regularly evaluates streets where sidewalks are needed most and prioritizes projects based on pedestrian traffic and safety concerns.

cards.headline: Sebastian completes Cresswind annexations
cards.teaser: The city of Sebastian has finalized annexations related to the Cresswind development, expanding city boundaries and services.
cards.body:
Sebastian has completed annexation proceedings for properties associated with the Cresswind development. The finalized annexations bring additional land into the city limits and extend municipal services to the area.

Cresswind is a residential development that will now fall fully under Sebastian's jurisdiction. The annexation process involved review by city officials and follows standard procedures for incorporating new areas into the municipality.

The completed annexations mean residents in the annexed areas will receive city services and be subject to Sebastian city codes and regulations. Annexations typically occur when developments are built adjacent to city boundaries and both the property owners and city agree to bring the land under municipal control.

cards.headline: Vero Beach installs historical marker honoring Florida woman
cards.teaser: A historical marker has been placed in Vero Beach to commemorate a Florida woman and her contributions to the community.
cards.body:
Vero Beach has installed a new historical marker recognizing a Florida woman for her role in local history. The marker serves as a permanent commemoration of her life and legacy in the community.

Historical markers help preserve and share important stories from Florida's past. They educate residents and visitors about significant people, places, and events that shaped local communities.

The placement of the marker in Vero Beach adds to the area's collection of historical sites and commemorations. These markers are typically installed after research and review by historical societies or government agencies to ensure accuracy and significance.

cards.headline: High gas prices continue affecting Treasure Coast fishing and boating
cards.teaser: Elevated fuel prices are impacting fishing and boating activities along the Treasure Coast as residents face higher costs for recreational trips.
cards.body:
Florida gas prices remain high across the Treasure Coast, directly affecting local fishing and boating enthusiasts. The elevated fuel costs are making recreational trips on the water more expensive for residents who rely on boats for fishing and leisure activities.

The impact is particularly noticeable in coastal communities like Stuart, Jensen Beach, Fort Pierce, and Vero Beach where boating is a major part of the lifestyle. Higher fuel prices affect not only recreational boaters but also charter fishing operations and commercial fishermen who depend on fuel-efficient operations.

Boaters throughout the region are adjusting their habits in response to fuel costs, potentially making shorter trips or going out less frequently. The sustained high prices represent an ongoing challenge for the Treasure Coast's vibrant marine recreation community and fishing industry.

cards.headline: Florida city plans new marina at historic downtown site
cards.teaser: A Florida city is moving forward with plans to develop a new marina on a historic property near downtown.
cards.body:
A new marina is coming to a Florida city at a historic site located near the downtown area. The development will transform the waterfront location into a modern marina facility while acknowledging its historical significance.

Marina projects typically bring economic activity to downtown waterfront areas and provide additional boat access for residents and visitors. The historic nature of the site adds cultural value to the development.

The marina development represents investment in waterfront infrastructure and recreational facilities. Florida cities with water access often balance preservation of historic sites with new development that serves the boating community and attracts visitors to downtown areas.

cards.headline: Property value growth declining for four years in Florida county
cards.teaser: A Florida county has experienced declining property value growth over a four-year period, reflecting changing real estate market conditions.
cards.body:
Property value growth has been declining for four consecutive years in a Florida county. The sustained trend reflects shifts in the local real estate market and economic conditions affecting property valuations.

Property value trends directly impact county tax revenues and homeowners' property tax bills. Declining growth rates can signal market cooling or economic changes affecting demand for real estate in the area.

County property appraisers track these trends annually to establish property values for tax purposes. While values may still be increasing, a declining growth rate means properties are appreciating more slowly than in previous years.

hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff's Office announces arrests in Operation Hammer Time hardware store burglary ring
hero.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff's Office will hold a press conference today to discuss arrests in a series of hardware store burglaries that hit Stuart and other Treasure Coast communities.
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office is holding a press conference today at 2 p.m. to discuss recent arrests made during Operation Hammer Time. Last week, Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced the arrest of three men in connection with the burglaries: Johnny Batista, 19, Roberto Hernandez-Castro, 39, and Roberto Aldana Ferrera, 31.

According to an affidavit from the sheriff's office, hardware stores in Stuart, Fort Pierce, and Jupiter were targeted, along with stores in Lake Worth, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, West Palm Beach, and Broward County. Investigators say they have been looking into a large-scale burglary ring targeting businesses overnight from December 2025 to April 2026. The crews would use a sledgehammer or other blunt object to break the glass and often completed the thefts within minutes, before police arrived or alarms were triggered.

Investigators say the three men arrested are main members of the burglary crew. Batista is connected to the first known theft at Sewell Hardware in Stuart in December 2025. The sheriff's office says the arrests were made in connection with a series of hardware store burglaries both locally and across the state.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman loses home, irreplaceable photos of late son in lightning strike fire
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with almost nothing and destroying photos of her late son.
cards.body:
Rosa Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church last month when a utility worker stopped her outside to tell her he thought her house was on fire. St. Lucie County firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire.

Rivera lost clothes, furniture, and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son, who passed away three years ago. The damage left Rivera, who is uninsured and disabled, displaced. She is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home.

A GoFundMe has been set up to help Rivera rebuild. Despite everything, Rivera said she is holding onto gratitude that she was not inside when the fire broke out. A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced.

cards.headline: Jupiter makes history as 91 firefighters sworn in for town's first fire department
cards.teaser: For the first time in Jupiter's history, the town has its own fire department. Ninety-one firefighters took their oath of service Monday at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre.
cards.body:
The ceremony marked the culmination of more than two years of work building Jupiter Fire Rescue from the ground up. Fire Chief Darrel Donatto called it the most proud day of his 45-year career in the fire service. Among the newest members is Lieutenant Christian Lainhart, a sixth-generation Jupiter resident who served with Martin County Fire Rescue before seeing the chance to serve his hometown.

Donatto noted the deep local ties running through the new department's ranks. Twenty-nine people who joined Jupiter Fire Rescue are local hometown Jupiter residents who have come home to serve their community. Behind every firefighter is a family making sacrifices. Lainhart's wife Jessica, who also grew up in Jupiter, said there have been many Christmases and Thanksgivings where her husband has been working.

Jupiter's historic week is not over. Station 10 on U.S. 1, the community's newest fire station, will open for the first time Wednesday at 11 a.m. when a ribbon-cutting ceremony will be held.

cards.headline: Black bear spotted swimming through Port St. Lucie neighborhood
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police shared rare video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community before running toward nearby homes.
cards.body:
The video, posted on the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Facebook page, shows the large black bear navigating through residential waters in what officials described as seasonal behavior for Florida's black bear population. Port St. Lucie police stated that as Florida's black bears become more active this time of year in search of food, occasional sightings in residential neighborhoods can occur. While seeing a bear may be surprising, it is not necessarily cause for alarm.

According to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, bear sightings remain rare throughout most of the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County regions, making Tuesday's Port St. Lucie encounter particularly noteworthy for local residents. If residents spot a bear, authorities recommend maintaining significant distance, never approaching the animal, and avoiding any attempts to feed it. Port St. Lucie police advise residents to keep children and pets away from bears and secure potential food sources including garbage, pet food, and bird seed around their properties.

During unexpected bear encounters, officials stress remaining calm and avoiding running. Instead, residents should slowly back away while keeping the bear visible, speak in calm, firm tones, and ensure the animal has a clear escape route. Florida's black bears, once listed as threatened, have increasingly wandered into neighborhoods and private properties in recent years as the population has grown substantially following decades of conservation efforts.

cards.headline: Historic Boston House in Fort Pierce reopens as downtown dining destination
cards.teaser: The Boston House, a downtown Fort Pierce staple for more than a century, has officially reopened as a new dining experience, bringing fresh energy to a city working to redefine its future.
cards.body:
Built in 1909 along South Indian River Drive, the home is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has served a variety of roles over the decades. Now, its newest owners are working to preserve its past while reimagining its purpose. Co-owner Georgette Angelos said the goal is to make guests feel at home while honoring the building's legacy.

Originally built by an engineer for Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway, who later became St. Lucie County's third sheriff, the Boston House remains closely tied to the region's early development. During renovations, the owners intentionally preserved historic details, including low original ceilings and Florida-themed law books that nod to the home's past.

General manager Scott Laird said the revival of the property reflects broader momentum downtown. Fort Pierce has had a reputation, and they really have done a great job bringing new life to the downtown area, Laird said. Each room in the Boston House offers a distinct experience rooted in local history, blending preservation with a modern dining atmosphere.

cards.headline: Loxahatchee residents celebrate completion of new levee after 2012 Tropical Storm Isaac flooding
cards.teaser: Nearly fifteen years after devastating floods wrecked North Loxahatchee during Tropical Storm Isaac, a brand-new levee is finally complete, taller, wider, and safer than ever.
cards.body:
The failed levee back in 2012 left homes underwater, roads impassable, and residents stranded for days. Betty Argue, a longtime advocate with the Indian Trail Improvement District, remembers the uphill battle to secure funding for a critical upgrade. She told reporters funding never got final budget approval as lawmakers didn't see the project as a priority. In 2013, the state appropriated $4 million for Phase I, protecting mostly agricultural land. But the eastern portion shielding neighborhoods was left incomplete when funding dried up.

It would take years of lobbying, partnerships, and persistence from multiple organizations, local and state officials, and residents to finally secure the $10.4 million needed for Phase II, which stretches in total over 5 miles and now completes the levee system. Everett Mitchell still remembers watching from his front porch as the old levee collapsed during Isaac. We watched it breach. It was like a waterfall, Mitchell said. Water poured into homes, trapping neighbors inside. Some escaped on boats and canoes.

Mitchell attended the ribbon cutting ceremony and called the new levee beautiful, but says there are still weak spots that need to be taken care of. The new levee also provides a road across the canal for vehicles and bikers. Work is underway for a water control gate on the M-0 Canal as part of ongoing flood protection improvements in the area.

cards.headline: Five hospitalized after multi-vehicle crash, fire on I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: Five people were taken to hospitals Monday night after a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 northbound near Stuart sparked a vehicle fire, according to Martin.
cards.body:
Five people were taken to hospitals Monday night after a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 northbound near Stuart sparked a vehicle fire, according to Martin County Fire Rescue. The collision occurred just before 10 p.m. on I-95 northbound near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park.

Martin County Fire Rescue crews arrived to find one of the vehicles on fire and quickly extinguished the flames. Two people suffered traumatic injuries and were transported to the hospital, while three others sustained minor injuries and were also taken for medical treatment.

All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed while law enforcement investigated the crash. The closure affected traffic through the night as investigators worked to determine what caused the collision.

As of Tuesday morning, all lanes have reopened. The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the crash.

hero.headline: Heiress donates land adjacent to Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve to block development
hero.body:
An heiress is working to preserve natural land in Hobe Sound by purchasing property and donating it to conservation efforts. The donated land sits adjacent to the Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve, expanding protected habitat in the area.

The heiress has been actively buying land in Florida specifically to prevent development. By transferring ownership of these parcels to conservation organizations, she ensures the property remains undeveloped and protects the region's natural ecosystems.

The Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve serves as a protected habitat for native plants and wildlife. The additional acreage increases the size of the contiguous protected area, which benefits species that require larger territories and creates a more resilient natural buffer against development pressure in northern Martin County.

This donation represents a growing trend of private conservation efforts on the Treasure Coast, where development pressure continues to threaten remaining natural areas. The expanded preserve will remain accessible for residents who use the trails and natural areas for recreation and education.

cards.headline: Sebastian finalizes annexation of Cresswind development
cards.teaser: The city of Sebastian has completed the annexation process for Cresswind, a development that will now become part of the city limits.
cards.body:
Sebastian city officials have finalized the annexation of the Cresswind development, bringing the property officially within city boundaries. The annexation marks a significant expansion of Sebastian's municipal footprint and will add residents and property tax revenue to the city.

The Cresswind development represents a substantial addition to Sebastian's housing stock and population. With the annexation complete, city services including police, fire protection, water, sewer, and code enforcement will now extend to the new properties. The development will also contribute to the city's tax base, providing revenue for municipal operations.

Annexation decisions affect how quickly Sebastian grows and how city resources are allocated. Residents in annexed areas receive city services but also pay city taxes and follow Sebastian's municipal codes and ordinances. The completion of this process follows months of planning and negotiation between developers and city officials.

cards.headline: Property value growth declines for four straight years in Florida county
cards.teaser: A Florida county has seen property value growth slow down for four consecutive years, affecting tax revenues and the local real estate market.
cards.body:
Property value increases have declined for the fourth year in a row in one Florida county, signaling a cooling real estate market. The slowing growth affects how much revenue local governments collect from property taxes, which fund schools, roads, public safety, and other essential services.

Declining growth rates mean property values are still increasing, but at a slower pace than in previous years. This trend follows a period of rapid appreciation that drove property values to record highs across much of Florida. The slowdown reflects changing market conditions including higher interest rates, insurance costs, and shifting buyer demand.

Property tax revenues depend heavily on assessed values, so the slowing growth rate affects budget planning for county commissioners, school boards, and other taxing authorities. Local governments may need to adjust spending plans or consider millage rate changes to maintain service levels as the pace of value growth moderates.

cards.headline: Florida mall partially demolished as era ends
cards.teaser: Demolition has begun on a Florida mall, with photos capturing the shopping center during its heyday now circulating as the building comes down.
cards.body:
A Florida mall has been partially demolished, marking the end of an era for a shopping center that once served as a community gathering place. Photos from the mall's peak years show the contrast between its former bustling activity and its current state of demolition.

The demolition reflects broader changes in retail as shopping malls across Florida and the country face declining foot traffic due to online shopping and changing consumer habits. Many malls built during the shopping center boom of past decades have struggled to maintain occupancy as anchor stores close and smaller retailers leave.

The fate of the property after demolition will determine how the site contributes to the local economy going forward. Some former mall sites have been redeveloped as mixed-use projects with apartments, restaurants, and entertainment venues, while others become distribution centers or remain vacant. The transformation of mall properties affects nearby businesses, traffic patterns, and property values in surrounding neighborhoods.

cards.headline: Conservation effort continues as heiress purchases Florida land to prevent development
cards.teaser: An heiress has been buying land across Florida with the specific goal of stopping development and preserving natural areas.
cards.body:
A wealthy heiress is purchasing land throughout Florida as part of a conservation strategy aimed at preventing development. Her approach involves acquiring property that might otherwise be sold to developers, then transferring it to conservation organizations or keeping it undeveloped.

The land purchases represent a private conservation model that complements public land acquisition programs. While government agencies often face budget constraints and political considerations when buying conservation land, private buyers can move quickly and focus on properties that fill critical gaps in protected areas. The heiress targets parcels that face immediate development pressure or that connect existing preserves.

Florida continues to lose natural areas to development as population growth drives demand for housing and commercial space. Private conservation efforts like these help preserve habitat for wildlife, protect water resources, and maintain the natural character that attracts residents and tourists to the state. Each preserved parcel means less impervious surface, fewer demands on infrastructure, and more space for the ecosystems that support Florida's environment.

cards.headline: New French cafe opens in Cocoa Beach
cards.teaser: Cocoa Beach has a new French cafe serving residents and visitors on the Space Coast.
cards.body:
A new French cafe has opened its doors in Cocoa Beach, adding to the dining options available in the beachside community. The cafe brings French-inspired cuisine and atmosphere to the Space Coast area.

The opening represents another addition to Cocoa Beach's restaurant scene, which serves both local residents and the steady flow of tourists visiting the area's beaches and attractions. New restaurants create jobs and contribute to the local economy while giving residents more choices for dining out.

Cocoa Beach sits just north of the Treasure Coast in Brevard County, making it a destination for residents from Sebastian and Vero Beach who travel up the coast for beach visits or dining. The cafe joins other restaurants competing for customers in a market that depends heavily on both year-round residents and seasonal visitors.

cards.headline: Brevard County sees restaurant sales and new culinary businesses
cards.teaser: Several eateries are changing hands or opening in Brevard County, just north of the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
Brevard County's restaurant scene continues to evolve with multiple eateries up for sale and new culinary ventures opening. The changes reflect the dynamic nature of the food service industry, where ownership transitions and new concepts constantly reshape dining options.

Restaurant sales often signal both challenges and opportunities in the industry. Some owners sell because of retirement or changing priorities, while buyers see potential in existing locations with established customer bases. New restaurant openings demonstrate entrepreneur confidence in the local market and add variety to dining choices for residents.

Brevard County borders Indian River County to the north, making dining and business trends there relevant to Treasure Coast residents who frequently travel to Cocoa Beach, Melbourne, and other Brevard communities. The health of the restaurant industry serves as an indicator of broader economic conditions, consumer spending, and tourism activity across the region.

hero.headline: School bus driver arrested in Treasure Coast after second student comes forward with allegations
hero.body:
A Florida school bus driver has been arrested following allegations from a second student. The arrest comes after an initial complaint led to an investigation that has now expanded with additional allegations of lewd and lascivious molestation.

The second victim came forward after the initial arrest, prompting authorities to file additional charges. The case involves allegations of inappropriate conduct toward students who rode the school bus. Law enforcement officials took the driver into custody following the second complaint.

The arrest raises serious concerns for parents and school officials across the Treasure Coast region. School districts rely on bus drivers to safely transport thousands of students daily, and allegations of this nature prompt immediate action from both law enforcement and school administrators.

The investigation remains active as authorities work to determine if there may be additional victims. School officials are cooperating with law enforcement as the criminal case moves forward through the judicial system.

cards.headline: Four-vehicle crash shuts down northbound I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: A multi-vehicle collision closed northbound lanes of Interstate 95 in Martin County, disrupting traffic flow on the major highway that connects Treasure Coast communities.
cards.body:
Northbound Interstate 95 in Martin County was shut down following a four-vehicle crash. The collision blocked travel lanes on the highway that serves as the main north-south route through the Treasure Coast, connecting Stuart, Jensen Beach, and other Martin County communities to points north and south.

The crash affected the morning commute for residents traveling through Martin County. Interstate 95 is the primary highway for commuters and commercial traffic moving through the region, and closures on the route create significant backups and delays.

Authorities responded to the scene to clear the wreckage and investigate the cause of the collision. The highway closure forced drivers to seek alternate routes or wait for lanes to reopen as emergency crews worked to clear the roadway and restore normal traffic flow.

cards.headline: Property value growth declines for fourth straight year in Florida county
cards.teaser: A Florida county has seen property value growth decline for four consecutive years, a trend that affects tax revenue and local government budgets.
cards.body:
Property value growth has declined for the fourth year in a row in a Florida county. The continued decline in growth rates represents a significant trend in the local real estate market and has implications for county finances and services.

Property values directly affect the tax base that local governments rely on to fund schools, roads, public safety, and other essential services. While property values may still be increasing, the rate of growth has slowed each year for four years, which can constrain budget planning for county commissioners and school boards.

The slowing growth trend stands in contrast to the rapid appreciation many Florida communities experienced in recent years. Local officials must balance property tax rates with the revenue needed to maintain services as growth in the tax base moderates over time.

cards.headline: Property values see modest increase across Florida county
cards.teaser: A Florida county has recorded a modest increase in property values, providing local governments with a slightly larger tax base to fund services.
cards.body:
Property values across a Florida county have posted a modest increase according to recent assessments. The uptick in property values expands the tax base that funds county services, though the growth remains moderate compared to previous years.

Property assessments determine how much revenue local governments can collect through property taxes, which pay for schools, law enforcement, fire services, road maintenance, and other essential functions. Even modest increases provide additional resources for county budgets, though officials must carefully balance tax rates with the needs of property owners.

The property value increase reflects ongoing activity in the local real estate market. Homeowners across the county will see the updated valuations reflected in their tax assessments, which determine their annual property tax bills based on millage rates set by county commissioners, school boards, and other taxing authorities.

cards.headline: Florida lawmakers debate property tax proposal and its impact on local services
cards.teaser: State lawmakers are debating a property tax proposal that could affect how local governments across Florida, including Treasure Coast counties, fund services.
cards.body:
Florida lawmakers are debating a property tax proposal that could significantly impact local government services across the state. The discussion in the legislature centers on changes to property tax policy that would affect counties, cities, and school districts throughout Florida, including communities across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

Property taxes represent the primary revenue source for local governments, funding everything from schools and law enforcement to road maintenance and parks. Any changes to property tax policy at the state level directly affect the budgets that county commissioners and city councils have available to provide services to residents.

Local government officials closely monitor property tax legislation in Tallahassee because state policy decisions constrain how counties and cities can raise revenue. The outcome of the current debate will determine how much flexibility local officials have in setting tax rates and managing budgets in the coming years.

cards.headline: School year ends this week in Miami-Dade and Broward counties as Florida districts wrap up
cards.teaser: The school year is coming to a close this week in Miami-Dade and Broward counties, following the typical Florida school calendar that sees districts finish in late May and early June.
cards.body:
School ends this week in Miami-Dade and Broward counties as Florida school districts wrap up the academic year. The conclusion of classes in South Florida follows the standard school calendar used by most Florida districts, which typically run from August through late May or early June.

School calendars across Florida generally follow similar patterns, with the academic year beginning in mid to late August and concluding before the summer heat sets in. Districts across the Treasure Coast and throughout the state coordinate their calendars to align with state testing requirements and seasonal weather patterns.

The end of the school year marks the beginning of summer break for students and teachers across Florida. Families prepare for summer activities and camps while school administrators and teachers take time off before beginning preparations for the next academic year that will start in a few months.

cards.headline: Florida Trust for Historic Preservation announces 2026 endangered sites list
cards.teaser: The Florida Trust for Historic Preservation has released its 2026 list of 11 historic sites across the state that face threats and need protection efforts.
cards.body:
The Florida Trust for Historic Preservation has revealed its 2026 list of 11 endangered historic sites across Florida. The annual list highlights historic buildings, structures, and places that face threats from development, neglect, or other factors that could lead to their loss.

The 11 to Save list serves as a call to action for preservationists, local governments, and community members to protect important historic resources. Sites that make the list often receive increased attention and support for preservation efforts, helping to save structures that tell the story of Florida's past.

Historic preservation groups use the annual list to raise awareness about threatened sites and mobilize resources to protect them. The Florida Trust works with local communities, property owners, and government agencies to find solutions that preserve historic buildings while allowing for appropriate development and reuse.

hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff's Office to hold press conference on hardware store theft investigation
hero.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff's Office has scheduled a press conference regarding Operation Hammer Time, an investigation into a series of hardware store thefts across the county.
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced it will hold a press conference Tuesday afternoon regarding Operation Hammer Time, an investigation targeting hardware store thefts in the area. The briefing is scheduled to provide information about the scope of the investigation and any arrests or charges resulting from the operation.

Hardware stores across Martin County have been targeted in a series of thefts, prompting law enforcement to launch the coordinated investigation. The sheriff's office chose the name Operation Hammer Time in reference to the type of merchandise and businesses affected by the crime spree.

Martin County communities including Stuart, Jensen Beach, Palm City, and Hobe Sound rely on local hardware stores for home improvement supplies and professional contracting needs. Retail theft affects not only business owners but also customers who may face higher prices as stores attempt to offset losses from stolen inventory.

cards.headline: Second alleged victim comes forward in St. Lucie County bus driver molestation case
cards.teaser: A second alleged victim has come forward in a molestation case involving a St. Lucie County school bus driver, expanding the scope of the investigation.
cards.body:
A second alleged victim has stepped forward in a molestation investigation involving a school bus driver in St. Lucie County. The new allegation adds another dimension to a case that has already raised concerns among parents and school officials across the county.

The case involves a bus driver who transports students in St. Lucie County, which includes Port St. Lucie and Fort Pierce. School bus drivers are entrusted with the safety and wellbeing of children during their daily commutes to and from school, making allegations of abuse particularly troubling for families throughout the community.

The investigation continues as authorities work to determine the full extent of the allegations. St. Lucie County schools serve thousands of students who rely on bus transportation each day, and cases like this highlight the importance of thorough background checks and ongoing supervision of school employees who work directly with children.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man accused of posing as courier in $44,400 scam targeting elderly woman
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie man faces accusations of posing as a courier in a sophisticated scheme that drained more than $44,000 from a 73-year-old woman through remote access and fake refund tactics.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man is accused of serving as a courier in an elaborate scam that stole $44,400 from a 73-year-old Boynton Beach woman. The scheme involved remote access to the victim's computer, a fake refund scenario, and the use of pickup codes to extract funds.

The scam represents a growing trend of fraud targeting elderly residents across South Florida, including the Treasure Coast. Criminals use sophisticated tactics including remote computer access to gain control of victims' financial accounts, often posing as legitimate customer service representatives or technical support staff. Once they establish trust and access, they manufacture scenarios requiring the victim to send money.

Port St. Lucie and surrounding St. Lucie County communities have seen an increase in such fraud cases, with law enforcement urging residents, particularly older adults, to be cautious about unsolicited phone calls or emails requesting remote computer access. The case serves as a reminder that legitimate businesses will never ask customers to provide remote access to their computers or to send money through couriers as part of refund processes.

cards.headline: Prescribed burn planned for up to 3,500 acres north of Lake Okeechobee this week
cards.teaser: The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission announced plans for a prescribed burn covering up to 3,500 acres on the north side of Lake Okeechobee this week.
cards.body:
The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission will conduct a prescribed burn on the north side of Lake Okeechobee this week, potentially affecting up to 3,500 acres of marsh. The controlled burn is part of ongoing land management efforts in the region.

Prescribed burns are an important tool for managing Florida's natural ecosystems, reducing wildfire risk, and promoting healthy habitat for wildlife. The burns clear accumulated vegetation and dead plant material that could otherwise fuel uncontrolled wildfires during dry conditions. The north Lake Okeechobee marsh provides critical habitat for birds and other wildlife.

Residents in communities surrounding Lake Okeechobee, including areas of Martin and St. Lucie counties, may notice smoke from the controlled burn. The Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission coordinates such burns carefully, monitoring weather conditions to ensure smoke disperses safely and fire remains contained within the planned burn area. Drivers in the region should be alert for reduced visibility if smoke drifts across roadways.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast high school graduates celebrate 2026 commencement ceremonies
cards.teaser: High schools across the Treasure Coast are holding graduation ceremonies for the Class of 2026, marking a milestone for students in Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.
cards.body:
Graduation season is underway across the Treasure Coast as high schools celebrate the Class of 2026. Students in Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties are receiving diplomas and preparing for the next chapters of their lives, whether that means college, vocational training, military service, or entering the workforce.

High school graduations represent major community events in Treasure Coast towns, bringing together families, educators, and local officials to honor student achievement. Schools including those in Stuart, Port St. Lucie, Fort Pierce, Vero Beach, and Sebastian are hosting ceremonies throughout late May and early June.

The graduation schedule varies by school and district, with ceremonies typically held at school stadiums, performing arts centers, or other large venues capable of accommodating graduates and their guests. The Class of 2026 faced unique challenges during their high school years and now joins the workforce and higher education institutions as they begin their adult lives.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast readers vote on all-time best girls basketball players
cards.teaser: A poll is underway asking Treasure Coast residents to vote on the region's all-time best girls basketball players, celebrating the area's rich high school basketball tradition.
cards.body:
Treasure Coast sports fans have the opportunity to vote on the all-time best girls basketball players from the region. The poll highlights the strong tradition of girls basketball at high schools across Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties.

High school basketball is a major part of community life on the Treasure Coast, with teams from Stuart, Port St. Lucie, Fort Pierce, Vero Beach, and other towns regularly producing talented athletes who go on to play at the college level. The region has developed numerous standout players over the years who have made their marks both locally and at higher levels of competition.

The voting process allows residents to celebrate local athletic excellence and remember the players who represented their schools and communities with distinction on the basketball court. Girls basketball programs across the Treasure Coast continue to develop young athletes, building on the legacy of past stars who paved the way for current and future generations.

cards.headline: 4-vehicle crash shuts down northbound I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: A multi-vehicle crash closed northbound lanes of Interstate 95 in Martin County on Tuesday morning, disrupting traffic along one of the Treasure Coast's busiest.
cards.body:
A multi-vehicle crash closed northbound lanes of Interstate 95 in Martin County on Tuesday morning, disrupting traffic along one of the Treasure Coast's busiest corridors.

The crash involved four vehicles and forced authorities to shut down the northbound lanes of I-95. The closure caused significant delays for commuters traveling through Martin County during the morning hours.

Martin County is a major thoroughfare for travelers moving between South Florida and points north along the Treasure Coast. I-95 serves as the primary north-south route through the region, connecting communities including Stuart, Jensen Beach, and Palm City to destinations throughout Florida.

Authorities worked to clear the crash scene and reopen the affected lanes. The incident underscores the ongoing traffic challenges faced by residents and travelers along the I-95 corridor through Martin County, where crashes can quickly create bottlenecks affecting thousands of motorists.

hero.headline: Palm Beach Gardens Sixth Graders Lead Free Computer Building Camp for Treasure Coast Youth
hero.body:
A group of sixth graders in Palm Beach Gardens is teaching their peers how to build computers and learn artificial intelligence basics this week at The Weiss School. The Kids Teaching Kids Academy, founded by 12-year-old Heath Neer, has grown from five students last year to 20 participants this summer, with five student instructors leading the free program.

The camp runs June 1-4 and brings together students from Palm Beach Gardens, West Palm Beach and Riviera Beach. Participants get hands-on experience assembling computers that they take home at no cost, plus lessons on fundamental AI concepts. The program is entirely peer-led, with support from The Weiss School and parent volunteers.

The initiative addresses the uneven access to technology tools and knowledge across the region. By using donated computer parts and community support to keep costs down, organizers ensure that students who might not otherwise have access to a computer can build and keep one. Student instructors wear matching camp shirts and hats, creating a team atmosphere.

With the first day already underway, instructors plan to complete each computer build and move into demonstrations of AI applications by the end of the week. Organizers hope the program's success will encourage similar peer-led models to spread across Palm Beach County, empowering more young people to teach and learn technology skills together.

cards.headline: Armory Art Center Opens Summer Camp Registration in West Palm Beach
cards.teaser: The Armory Art Center in West Palm Beach has launched its summer camp lineup, offering art programs for all ages from young children through adults.
cards.body:
The Armory Art Center is kicking off summer with a full schedule of camps and creative programs designed for artists of all ages, according to Education Director Vita Litvak. The offerings range from splatter painting inspired by mid-20th-century art movements to workshops exploring global art styles and cultures.

Summer camp sessions run in various formats through August, with registration now open at armoryart.org. The center offers scholarships to ensure cost is not a barrier for young artists who want to participate. The programs span from youth camps to adult intensive workshops.

The broad range of offerings reflects a growing trend of accessible, community-based creativity as arts organizations across Palm Beach County work to reach residents seeking enrichment close to home during summer break.

cards.headline: Junior Lifeguard Camp Opens on Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: The first two weeks of Junior Lifeguard Camp are now underway on the Treasure Coast, offering young residents water safety and lifeguard training.
cards.body:
Weeks one and two of Junior Lifeguard Camp are taking place on the Treasure Coast, providing local youth with hands-on training in water safety and lifeguarding skills. The program gives participants the chance to learn essential beach and pool safety techniques while building physical fitness and confidence in the water.

Junior lifeguard programs have become a summer staple across Florida's coastal communities, preparing the next generation of ocean-safety professionals. The camps typically cover CPR, first aid, swimming techniques, rescue procedures, and ocean awareness.

These early summer sessions set the stage for what many communities consider vital youth programming, combining recreation with practical life skills that can lead to summer employment opportunities as participants grow older.

cards.headline: Kennedy Space Center Plans July-August Events Celebrating America's 250th Anniversary
cards.teaser: Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex has announced its July through August 2026 schedule featuring special events celebrating the nation's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, located about an hour north of the Treasure Coast in Brevard County, has rolled out its summer schedule celebrating America's 250th anniversary. The July through August 2026 programming will feature special events and space history experiences tied to the milestone.

The proximity of Kennedy Space Center makes it a popular destination for Treasure Coast families seeking educational summer outings. The complex regularly draws visitors from Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties who want to experience Florida's role in space exploration history.

The 250th anniversary programming adds a patriotic dimension to the center's usual offerings of rocket launches, astronaut encounters, and interactive exhibits. Treasure Coast residents planning summer trips can expect the facility to be busy during peak vacation months.

cards.headline: Zoetic Stage's Stuart Meltzer Receives George Abbott Award
cards.teaser: Stuart Meltzer of Zoetic Stage has been honored with the George Abbott Award for Excellence in Theatre, recognizing his contributions to South Florida performing arts.
cards.body:
Stuart Meltzer, a key figure at Zoetic Stage, has earned the George Abbott Award for Excellence in Theatre. The recognition honors his work in South Florida's theater community and contributions to the performing arts scene.

The George Abbott Awards are among the most prestigious honors in regional theater, named for the legendary Broadway director and producer. Recipients are recognized for their sustained excellence and impact on theatrical productions and theater development.

While Zoetic Stage is based in Miami, the recognition reflects the interconnected nature of South Florida's arts community, which extends from Miami-Dade through Palm Beach counties. Theater professionals and arts patrons across the region, including the Treasure Coast, often follow and support productions throughout the broader South Florida cultural corridor.

cards.headline: John Brewster Music to Perform at Hudson's Sunset Sunday
cards.teaser: John Brewster Music will perform at a Sunset Sunday event at Hudson's, offering live entertainment for Treasure Coast residents.
cards.body:
Live music is coming to Hudson's with a Sunset Sunday performance by John Brewster Music. The event offers Treasure Coast residents an opportunity to enjoy local entertainment in a relaxed evening setting.

Sunset performances have become a staple of coastal Florida life, combining music with the region's natural beauty as the sun sets over the water. These gatherings provide a family-friendly atmosphere where residents can unwind and connect with their community.

Local venues throughout Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties regularly host similar events during summer months, supporting both musicians and the hospitality businesses that anchor waterfront entertainment districts. Live music nights contribute to the area's appeal as a destination for both residents and visitors seeking authentic Florida experiences.

cards.headline: Linda Ronstadt Experience Returns to Treasure Coast in January 2027
cards.teaser: The Linda Ronstadt Experience tribute show will return to the Treasure Coast on Friday, January 15, 2027, giving fans advance notice to plan.
cards.body:
Fans of Linda Ronstadt can mark their calendars for January 15, 2027, when The Linda Ronstadt Experience tribute show returns to the Treasure Coast. The advance announcement gives residents nearly eight months to plan for the performance.

Tribute shows celebrating iconic musicians have become popular entertainment options across Florida, offering audiences the chance to hear beloved songs performed live. The Linda Ronstadt Experience recreates the music of the legendary singer whose career spanned rock, country, Latin and pop genres.

Early announcements of winter season entertainment help Treasure Coast venues build audiences and give residents something to look forward to during the busy fall and holiday seasons. The January date falls during the region's peak season when northern visitors and year-round residents alike seek cultural and entertainment activities.

hero.headline: Florida Legislature approves property tax cut amendment for November ballot
hero.body:
The Florida Legislature completed its special session Tuesday by approving a tweaked version of Governor Ron DeSantis's proposed property tax cut constitutional amendment. The measure will now go before Florida voters in November.

Lawmakers reconvened for the second day of the special session focused solely on property taxes. The Legislature made modifications to the governor's original proposal before advancing it to a floor vote. Both chambers approved the amended version Tuesday afternoon, sending the constitutional amendment to the ballot for statewide consideration.

The special session brought together members from across Florida to address property tax concerns affecting homeowners and businesses statewide. The National Federation of Independent Business, whose members represent every industry in Florida, has been tracking the legislative developments. Business owners and property owners across the state have been watching the session closely as property tax relief measures could affect their bottom lines.

Florida voters will have the final say on the property tax amendment when they head to the polls in November. Constitutional amendments in Florida require voter approval to take effect. The outcome of the vote will determine whether property tax cuts become part of the state constitution, potentially affecting tax bills for millions of Florida property owners. The Legislature's completion of the special session marks a significant step in the process, though the ultimate decision now rests with the electorate.

cards.headline: Florida becomes first state to sue OpenAI over child safety concerns
cards.teaser: Florida has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, marking the first state-level legal action against the artificial intelligence company over child safety risks.
cards.body:
Florida broke new ground Tuesday by becoming the first state in the nation to file a lawsuit against OpenAI over concerns related to child safety. The legal action represents a significant escalation in state-level oversight of artificial intelligence companies and their potential risks to minors.

The lawsuit addresses child safety risks associated with OpenAI's technology, though the state's specific allegations were not detailed in available reports. Florida's decision to pursue legal action could set a precedent for other states considering similar measures against AI companies.

The case comes as both state and federal governments grapple with how to regulate rapidly advancing artificial intelligence technology. The Trump administration has separately asked leading AI developers to voluntarily submit their most capable models for government cybersecurity tests before public release, indicating growing government scrutiny of the AI industry across multiple fronts.

cards.headline: Pasco County Fire Rescue saves owl trapped between tree trunks
cards.teaser: A Pasco County Fire Rescue crew came to the aid of an owl that became stuck between tree trunks in an unusual animal rescue.
cards.body:
Pasco County Fire Rescue crews responded to an unusual call Tuesday when an owl became wedged between two tree trunks and could not free itself. The rescue crew successfully freed the trapped bird in the incident.

The rescue highlights the varied emergency calls that Florida fire departments handle beyond traditional fire and medical responses. Wildlife rescues are not uncommon in Florida, where diverse animal species frequently interact with residential areas.

Pasco County Fire Rescue teams are trained to handle animal emergencies alongside their standard emergency response duties. The owl was freed from its predicament thanks to the crew's intervention, allowing the bird to return to its natural habitat.

cards.headline: Florida deputies stop runaway boat with hook after children thrown from vessel
cards.teaser: Florida law enforcement used a boat hook to stop a runaway vessel after children were thrown from the boat in a water emergency.
cards.body:
Florida deputies responded to a dangerous situation on the water when children were thrown from a boat that subsequently became a runaway vessel. The quick-thinking law enforcement officers used a hook to stop the out-of-control boat.

The incident required immediate action to prevent further danger on the water. Deputies were able to secure the runaway vessel using the hook technique, bringing the situation under control. Video of the rescue captured the dramatic moments as officers worked to stop the boat.

Boating safety remains a critical concern in Florida, where waterways are heavily used for recreation and transportation. The state's extensive coastline and inland waterways see frequent boat traffic, and emergency responders regularly train for water-based rescue scenarios. The quick response by deputies prevented what could have been a more serious incident.

cards.headline: Florida's three major college baseball programs all eliminated in NCAA regionals
cards.teaser: Florida's top three college baseball programs all failed to advance past the NCAA regional round, marking a disappointing postseason for the state.
cards.body:
College baseball teams from Florida had a postseason to forget as the state's "Big 3" programs all failed to advance beyond the NCAA regional round. The early eliminations represent a rare collective struggle for Florida's powerhouse baseball programs.

Florida has long been considered a hotbed for college baseball talent, with multiple programs regularly competing for national championships. The simultaneous early exits of the state's three major programs mark an unusual outcome for Florida collegiate baseball.

The regional round losses bring an end to the 2026 season for these Florida programs earlier than expected. College baseball in the state typically sees strong performances from multiple teams advancing deep into the postseason tournament, making this year's results particularly notable for Florida baseball fans and programs.

cards.headline: Vernon Hargreaves III named to University of Florida Athletic Hall of Fame
cards.teaser: Former Florida Gators standout Vernon Hargreaves III has been selected for induction into the 2026 UF Athletic Hall of Fame class.
cards.body:
The University of Florida announced that Vernon Hargreaves III will be inducted into the 2026 UF Athletic Hall of Fame class. The selection honors Hargreaves's achievements during his time with the Gators football program.

Hargreaves played cornerback for Florida and was widely regarded as one of the top defensive backs in college football during his career with the Gators. His selection to the Athletic Hall of Fame recognizes his contributions to one of the state's most prominent college athletic programs.

The UF Athletic Hall of Fame honors former Gators athletes who achieved excellence in their respective sports while representing the university. Hargreaves joins other distinguished Florida athletes who have been recognized for their impact on Gators athletics. The formal induction ceremony for the 2026 class will take place later this year.

cards.headline: Florida Gators goalie Condon selected to Australian National Team
cards.teaser: A current Florida Gators athlete has earned selection to the Australian National Team, representing international recognition for the university's athletic program.
cards.body:
Condon, a member of the University of Florida Gators athletic program, has been selected to represent Australia on the national team. The selection represents a significant achievement for both the athlete and the Florida program.

The announcement adds to the international credentials of Florida's athletic department, which regularly produces athletes who compete at the highest levels of their sports. Having athletes selected for national team duty brings prestige to university programs and demonstrates the quality of competition and training available.

Condon will balance duties with both the Australian National Team and commitments to the University of Florida. Many college athletes who earn national team selection face scheduling challenges as they represent their countries while maintaining their collegiate eligibility and team responsibilities.

hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff's Office announces arrests in Operation Hammer Time hardware store burglary ring
hero.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff's Office held a press conference Tuesday to discuss arrests in a multi-county burglary operation that targeted hardware stores including Sewell Hardware in Stuart.
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced arrests in Operation Hammer Time, a case involving a series of hardware store burglaries across Florida. Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced last week the arrest of three men in connection with the burglaries: Johnny Batista, 19, Roberto Hernandez-Castro, 39, and Roberto Aldana Ferrera, 31.

According to an affidavit from the sheriff's office, hardware stores in Stuart, Lake Worth, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, West Palm Beach, Fort Pierce and Jupiter were targeted, as were stores in Broward County. Investigators say they have been looking into a large-scale burglary ring targeting businesses overnight from December 2025 to April 2026. The burglary crews would use a sledgehammer or other blunt object to break the glass and would often complete the thefts within minutes, before police arrived or alarms were triggered.

Investigators say the three men arrested are main members of the burglary crew. Batista is connected to the first known theft at Sewell Hardware in Stuart in December 2025. The sheriff's office held a press conference at 2 p.m. Tuesday to provide additional details about the investigation and arrests.

cards.headline: Heiress donates land adjacent to Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve
cards.teaser: An heiress has donated land adjacent to the Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve, adding to the protected natural area in Martin County.
cards.body:
A significant land donation has been made to expand protected natural areas near the Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve in Martin County. An heiress has donated property adjacent to the existing preserve, which protects one of the region's most ecologically important scrub habitats.

The Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve is home to rare and threatened species that depend on Florida's unique scrub ecosystem. The preserve provides critical habitat for wildlife and offers educational opportunities for residents and visitors interested in the area's natural heritage.

The donation represents a growing trend of private conservation efforts in Martin County, where development pressure continues to threaten natural areas. The additional land will help ensure long-term protection of the scrub ecosystem and the species that depend on it.

cards.headline: Injury crash on Florida's Turnpike causes traffic delays in Martin County
cards.teaser: First responders worked the scene of a vehicle crash on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County that caused traffic delays.
cards.body:
A crash on Florida's Turnpike in Martin County brought first responders to the scene and resulted in traffic delays for motorists traveling through the area. The incident involved injuries, prompting an emergency response.

The crash added to a busy period for Martin County emergency responders, who also dealt with a separate multi-vehicle collision on Interstate 95 that resulted in five hospitalizations and a vehicle fire. Both incidents affected major north-south routes through the county.

Florida's Turnpike serves as a critical transportation corridor for residents and travelers moving through Martin County. Crashes on the turnpike typically result in significant delays as emergency crews work to clear the scene and investigate the circumstances.

cards.headline: Stuart getting new marina on historic downtown site
cards.teaser: A Florida city is developing a new marina on a historic site near downtown, bringing additional waterfront access and services to the area.
cards.body:
Stuart is moving forward with plans for a new marina on a historic site near downtown. The development will bring additional waterfront access and boating services to the Martin County city, which has long been known for its connection to the St. Lucie River and the Intracoastal Waterway.

The marina project represents continued investment in Stuart's downtown waterfront area, which has seen growing interest from businesses and residents in recent years. The historic nature of the site adds significance to the development, connecting the city's maritime heritage with modern amenities.

Stuart's location on the St. Lucie River makes it a popular destination for boaters traveling along Florida's east coast. The new marina will provide additional docking space and services for both local boat owners and visitors passing through the area.

cards.headline: Prescribed burn planned for up to 3,500 acres on north side of Lake Okeechobee
cards.teaser: The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission announced plans for a prescribed burn covering up to 3,500 acres of marsh on the north side of Lake Okeechobee this week.
cards.body:
The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission announced Tuesday that it is planning a prescribed burn on the north side of Lake Okeechobee this week. The controlled burn could cover up to 3,500 acres of marsh area surrounding the massive lake.

Prescribed burns are a standard land management tool used to maintain healthy ecosystems, reduce the buildup of flammable vegetation, and promote the growth of native plants. The burns are carefully planned and executed under specific weather conditions to ensure safety and effectiveness.

Residents near the burn area may see smoke and should be aware of the planned activity. Lake Okeechobee, which borders Martin County to the west, is a critical water resource for the region and supports diverse wildlife habitats that benefit from periodic controlled burning.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man accused of posing as courier in $44,000 scam targeting elderly woman
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie man faces accusations of posing as a courier in a sophisticated scheme that tricked a 73-year-old Boynton Beach woman out of more than $44,000.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man is accused of posing as a courier in a sophisticated scam that drained $44,400 from a 73-year-old Boynton Beach woman. The scheme involved remote access, a fake refund claim, and a pickup code to complete the theft.

The case highlights ongoing concerns about scams targeting elderly residents across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Scammers often use elaborate schemes that involve multiple steps and impersonation of trusted entities or officials to gain victims' confidence.

Law enforcement officials regularly warn residents, particularly seniors, to be cautious about unsolicited contacts requesting remote access to computers, personal information, or money. Victims are encouraged to verify the legitimacy of any request by contacting companies or agencies directly using known phone numbers rather than responding to unexpected calls or messages.

cards.headline: Five hospitalized after multi-vehicle crash and fire shuts down I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: Five people were taken to the hospital Monday night following a multi-vehicle collision on Interstate 95 northbound that sparked a vehicle fire near Stuart.
cards.body:
Five people were taken to the hospital Monday night following a multi-vehicle collision on Interstate 95 northbound that sparked a vehicle fire near Stuart. The crash occurred just before 10 p.m. near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park.

Martin County Fire Rescue crews responded to the scene and found one of the vehicles engulfed in flames. Firefighters quickly extinguished the blaze. Two people suffered traumatic injuries and were transported to the hospital, while three others sustained minor injuries and were also taken for medical treatment.

All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed while law enforcement investigated the crash scene. The closure affected evening commuters traveling through Martin County on one of the area's busiest highways.

As of Tuesday morning, all northbound lanes have reopened to traffic. The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the circumstances that led to the collision.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie daughter charged with attempted murder after setting fire to bedroom door with mother inside
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman faces charges of attempted murder, arson and resisting arrest after police say she set fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was trapped inside Sunday night. Michelle Picard, 26, is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on $510,000 bond following the incident in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard.

Port St. Lucie Police Department officers responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire around 9:05 p.m. Sunday. The victim noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire, according to police. Investigators say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames.

The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background. Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her, but she resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg. Another officer required treatment for smoke inhalation. Both officers were treated at a local hospital and released. The victim was also hospitalized for treatment of injuries sustained during the incident.

Fire investigators from the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Criminal Investigations Division, Crime Scene Investigators, St. Lucie County Fire District and the State Fire Marshal's Office determined the blaze was intentionally set. The fire damaged the residence, prompting the American Red Cross to assist the victim with temporary housing and support services. Police emphasized this was an isolated domestic incident and there is no ongoing threat to the community.

cards.headline: North Miami man arrested after attempted armed kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church
