cards.teaser: A 64-year-old man faces multiple felony charges after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman at gunpoint in a Port St. Lucie church parking lot Sunday morning. Witnesses intervened to stop the incident.
cards.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman in the parking lot of First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard. The incident unfolded around 10:49 a.m. Sunday when Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached her despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

Police say Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim through the parking lot and physically restraining her.

Zamora was located and arrested without incident Sunday evening at a residence in Hialeah by Port St. Lucie Police and U.S. Marshals. The investigation revealed Zamora is a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Zamora faces five felony charges, including attempted kidnapping with a firearm, aggravated assault and battery of a person over 65. He is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on a $745,000 bond.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman displaced after lightning strike destroys home, loses photos of late son
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera returned from church last month to find her Fort Pierce home on fire after a lightning strike. Now uninsured and displaced, she lost irreplaceable belongings including photos of her son who passed away three years ago.
cards.body:
Rosa Rivera is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her Fort Pierce home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage and almost nothing left. When Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church, a utility worker stopped her outside to tell her the house was on fire. St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire.

Walking into her damaged home left Rivera stunned. She lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home.

A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera said she is holding onto gratitude that she was not inside when the fire broke out. A GoFundMe has been set up to help Rivera rebuild.

cards.headline: Second victim comes forward against former St. Lucie County school bus driver facing molestation charges
cards.teaser: Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie now faces an additional battery charge after a second victim came forward in an investigation that began in March when a 9-year-old student reported inappropriate conduct on the school bus.
cards.body:
Former St. Lucie County school bus driver Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie is facing an additional charge after a second victim came forward in an ongoing investigation into allegations of inappropriate conduct with children. Garcia was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 when the second victim came forward with additional information for investigators. This comes after his initial arrest March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age.

The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus. During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The case was then referred to the Criminal Investigations Division, leading to Garcia's initial arrest two days later on March 6.

The Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward. Anyone with information related to this case can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at 772-462-7300 or email CrimeTips@stluciesheriff.gov.

cards.headline: Historic Boston House in Fort Pierce reopens as downtown dining destination
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce landmark built in 1909 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places has officially reopened as a new dining experience, preserving its past while bringing fresh energy to downtown.
cards.body:
The Boston House, a downtown Fort Pierce staple for more than a century, is entering a new chapter as a new dining destination. Built in 1909 along South Indian River Drive, the home is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has served a variety of roles over the decades. Now, its newest owners are working to preserve its past while reimagining its purpose. Co-owner Georgette Angelos said Fort Pierce is eclectic, artistic, with deep, beautiful history, and the goal behind the historic doors is to make guests feel at home while honoring the building's legacy.

Originally built by an engineer for Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway, who later became St. Lucie County's third sheriff, the Boston House remains closely tied to the region's early development. During renovations, the owners intentionally preserved historic details, including low original ceilings and Florida-themed law books that nod to the home's past. General manager Scott Laird said the revival of the property reflects broader momentum downtown, noting that Fort Pierce has had a reputation and they really have done a great job bringing new life to the downtown area.

Each room in the Boston House offers a distinct experience rooted in local history, blending preservation with a modern dining atmosphere. Laird said holding onto the greatness in the area and shining a spotlight on it is important. The Boston House now stands as both a historic landmark and a renewed gathering place serving up a new chapter for downtown Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Black bear spotted swimming through Port St. Lucie neighborhood
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police shared rare video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community before running toward nearby homes, marking an unusual wildlife sighting along the Treasure Coast.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police shared rare video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community before exiting the water and running toward nearby homes. The video, posted on the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Facebook page, shows the large black bear navigating through residential waters in what officials described as seasonal behavior for Florida's black bear population. According to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission, bear sightings remain rare throughout most of the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County regions, making Tuesday's Port St. Lucie encounter particularly noteworthy for local residents.

Port St. Lucie police stated on Facebook that as Florida's black bears become more active this time of year in search of food, occasional sightings in residential neighborhoods can occur. While seeing a bear may be surprising, it is not necessarily cause for alarm, officials said. Wildlife officials emphasize specific protocols when encountering black bears in residential areas. If residents spot a bear, authorities recommend maintaining significant distance, never approaching the animal, and avoiding any attempts to feed it. Port St. Lucie police advise residents to keep children and pets away from bears and secure potential food sources including garbage, pet food and bird seed around their properties.

Florida's black bears, once listed as threatened, have increasingly wandered into neighborhoods and private properties in recent years, particularly affecting rural areas of north and central Florida, according to The Associated Press. This population recovery follows decades of conservation efforts, though it has led to more frequent human-wildlife interactions across the state. During unexpected bear encounters, officials stress remaining calm and avoiding running. Instead, residents should slowly back away while keeping the bear visible, speak in calm, firm tones, and ensure the animal has a clear escape route.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District honors fallen firefighter Connor Whitehead
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District held a memorial service to honor firefighter Connor Whitehead following his death.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District honored firefighter Connor Whitehead after his death, according to WPBF. The district held a memorial service recognizing Whitehead's service to the community and his fellow firefighters.

Whitehead's death represents a loss for the St. Lucie County Fire District and the broader Treasure Coast firefighting community. Fire service personnel and community members gathered to pay their respects to Whitehead and support his family during this time. The memorial service provided an opportunity for colleagues and residents to recognize his dedication to protecting St. Lucie County residents.

The St. Lucie County Fire District serves communities throughout the county, responding to fires, medical emergencies and other public safety incidents. Firefighters like Whitehead play a critical role in keeping Treasure Coast residents safe.

hero.headline: Body of suspect found after double homicide at Vero Beach library
hero.body:
The body of a suspect who killed his wife and another man at a Vero Beach library has been found, authorities report. The suspect had escaped into the ocean following the deadly incident at the library.

The double homicide occurred at a Vero Beach library facility, where the suspect killed his wife and one other man before fleeing the scene. Law enforcement pursued the suspect, who entered the ocean in an apparent escape attempt.

Search efforts by authorities focused on the coastal area where the suspect was last seen entering the water. The recovery of the suspect's body brings the manhunt to a close, though the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the killings continues.

The incident marks a tragic event for the Vero Beach community. The library serves as a public gathering place for residents throughout Indian River County, and the violent incident has impacted staff and patrons who use the facility regularly.

cards.headline: Indian River Mall demolition underway as former Macy's anchor store comes down
cards.teaser: Demolition has begun at Indian River Mall, with the former Macy's anchor store being torn down as part of a major redevelopment project.
cards.body:
The Indian River Mall is undergoing partial demolition, with work beginning on the former Macy's anchor store. Photos from the mall's earlier years show the retail center during its peak as a shopping destination for Indian River County residents.

The demolition marks the start of a transformation for the retail property, which has served the Vero Beach area for decades. The former anchor store is the first major structure to be removed as part of the redevelopment plans for the site.

New renderings show what the redeveloped Indian River Mall could look like after demolition is complete. The project represents a significant change for the retail landscape in Indian River County, as the mall transitions from its traditional format to a new concept that reflects changing consumer habits and commercial real estate trends.

cards.headline: Sebastian finalizes annexations for Cresswind development
cards.teaser: The city of Sebastian has completed annexations related to the Cresswind development project.
cards.body:
Sebastian city officials have finalized annexation proceedings for properties associated with the Cresswind development. The annexations bring additional land into the city limits to accommodate the residential project.

The Cresswind development represents growth for Sebastian, adding new housing to the northern Indian River County community. Annexation allows the city to extend municipal services and jurisdiction to the development area.

The completion of the annexation process clears the way for continued development of the Cresswind project. Sebastian has seen increased residential growth in recent years, and the Cresswind development adds to the expansion of housing options in the area.

cards.headline: Vero Beach approves $190,000 for Iris Lane sidewalk project
cards.teaser: The city of Vero Beach has approved funding for a new sidewalk on Iris Lane, with a price tag of $190,000.
cards.body:
Vero Beach officials have approved a $190,000 project to construct a sidewalk along Iris Lane. The approval allows the city to move forward with the pedestrian infrastructure improvement.

The Iris Lane sidewalk project addresses pedestrian safety and walkability in the neighborhood. Sidewalk construction provides residents with safer routes for walking and connects neighborhoods to nearby destinations.

The $190,000 investment reflects the city's ongoing commitment to pedestrian infrastructure throughout Vero Beach. Similar projects have been undertaken in other residential areas to improve safety and accessibility for walkers and residents without vehicles.

cards.headline: Historical marker honors Florida woman in Vero Beach
cards.teaser: A historical marker has been placed in Vero Beach to commemorate a Florida woman's contributions.
cards.body:
Vero Beach has installed a historical marker recognizing a Florida woman whose legacy merits permanent commemoration. The marker adds to the historical markers throughout Indian River County that preserve local history.

Historical markers serve as educational tools for residents and visitors, highlighting important figures and events that shaped the community. The placement of the marker in Vero Beach ensures that future generations can learn about the woman's contributions.

The marker dedication reflects ongoing efforts to document and preserve local history throughout Indian River County. Community members and historians work together to identify significant figures and locations worthy of permanent recognition through the historical marker program.

cards.headline: Indian River County continues review of Racquet Club request
cards.teaser: Indian River County officials are continuing their review of a request related to the Racquet Club property.
cards.body:
Indian River County commissioners are continuing their consideration of a request involving the Racquet Club. The matter remains under review as officials evaluate the proposal.

The Racquet Club review is part of the county's regular land use and development oversight process. County staff and commissioners assess such requests based on zoning regulations, comprehensive plan compliance, and community impact.

The continued review indicates that commissioners need additional time or information before making a final decision on the Racquet Club matter. County officials regularly table or continue items to allow for further analysis or public input before voting on development proposals.

cards.headline: Indian River County restaurant inspections show one perfect score, one failure
cards.teaser: Health inspections of Indian River County restaurants resulted in one establishment receiving a perfect score while another failed its inspection.
cards.body:
One Indian River County restaurant earned a perfect score during recent health inspections, while another restaurant failed to meet state health standards. The inspections are conducted regularly by health officials to ensure food safety.

Restaurant health inspections evaluate cleanliness, food handling practices, temperature controls, and other factors that affect public health. A perfect score indicates full compliance with all state health regulations, while a failed inspection requires immediate corrective action.

Indian River County residents can access restaurant inspection reports to make informed decisions about where to dine. Failed inspections typically require follow-up visits to verify that violations have been corrected before the establishment can continue operating.
